messages:
maria: Hey team — DeltaForge asked for final committed GPU hours for their Dedicated plan. They gave a 3-month forecast with daily peak at 11-14:00 UTC, avg QPS 6.5, 95th with spikes to ~12 qps. Model mix: 60% 7B quant (fast), 40% 34B fp16. They want a hard SLA and a 99% latency p95 under 450ms. Thinking about buffer policy — do we do flat % or model-aware buffer?
kevin: flat % is easy but wasteful. model-aware buffer (reserve extra for heavier model mix) better. With 34B at 40% of traffic spikes, we should size for normal + headroom for sudden model shifts.
sachin: Quick math I ran in a notebook: avg tokens per request 180, avg token gen time per model: 7B-quant ~0.0009s/token on A100, 34B-fp16 ~0.004s/token on H100. Peak tokens/s = qps * tokens. At 12 qps that's ~2160 tokens/s. If 40% are 34B that's 864 tokens/s on heavy model. That needs roughly 1 H100 + margin. 7B traffic fits many A100 workers.
lena: DeltaForge wants a monthly committed hours quote. We should convert to committed GPUs * 24 * 30 but allow burst to a shared pool. Suggest commit = baseline steady-state (95th non-spike) and buffer = 20% cross-pool + up to 2 H100 burst.
dan: Curious about warmup/WARM cache times for 34B when a new instance serves first requests — cold starts push latency above SLA. How long to warm kv cache?
sachin: Cold-start for 34B model with cache empty ~6-10s for first few tokens, but after prefix caching it's fine. We should include a warm-up window in SLO doc and recommend a pre-warm for canaries.
caroline: From sales: DeltaForge pushes for a 10% buffer to avoid commit costs. They're sensitive to price; prefer commit lower if we can promise burst. We need a proposal that balances commit size and burst pricing.
maria: OK — let's draft two options: (A) conservative commit: baseline+25% buffer, dedicated H100x1 + A100 pool; (B) lean commit: baseline only + paid burst up to 3 H100-hours at premium. Need exact GPU-hours calc.
kevin: I sketched the GPU-hours. Example: baseline = 6 qps steady -> tokens/s = 1080 -> effective GPU throughput per A100 for mixed workload ~120k tokens/s (after batching). That implies baseline ~= 9 A100-equivalents (this is permissive rounding). Baseline GPU-hours/month = 9 * 24 * 30 = 6480 GPU-hours (A100). For H100, because 34B occupies larger share during peak we should commit 1 H100 and allow 1-2 as burst.
maria: Can you paste the calc snippet?
kevin: Sure:```python
# very rough
qps_peak = 12
tokens_per_req = 180
tokens_per_sec = qps_peak * tokens_per_req
# assume 40% heavy (34B), heavy throughput per H100 ~ 800 tokens/s
heavy_tokens = tokens_per_sec * 0.4
h100_needed = math.ceil(heavy_tokens / 800)
# remaining tokens handled by A100 pool at 120k tok/s per GPU
remaining_tokens = tokens_per_sec - heavy_tokens
a100_needed = math.ceil(remaining_tokens / 120000)
```
lena: That looks reasonable for a starting point. For quoting, convert to committed hours and show cost delta for buffer sizes 10/20/30%.
ops-bot: [infra-monitor] cluster-alert: us-west1-a A100 pool CPU pressure spiked 1.2x at 2026-03-15T11:03:22Z — normalized. No service impact.
kevin: Also need to call out region constraints: DeltaForge is multi-region but prefers eu-west1 primary. eu-west1 has fewer H100s available on our fleet; capacity lead-time is 7-10 days for dedicated H100s. That affects commit timelines.
maria: Good flag. For proposal include a lead-time clause and optional cross-region failover to us-west. Also propose a 15% short-notice buffer cost if they need immediate H100s.
caroline: Sales asks for two price tables: one inline with reserved hours and discounted rate; one for on-demand burst rate (x1.6). Show monthly committed A100-hours and H100-hours separately.
dan: Operational note — if we offer model-aware buffer, we must surface per-model routing rules in the console so customers can see how burst triggers. Add a runbook for scaling H100s and pre-warm steps (invoke warmup endpoint with sample traces).
sachin: Agreed. I'll prepare a short runbook snippet:```bash
# prewarm 34B on target pool
curl -X POST https://api.redwood/runwarm -d '{"model":"34B","prefixes":["Hello","Summarize"]}' -H "Authorization: Bearer ..."
```
maria: Great. Action items: sachin to produce final GPU-hour calc + runbook, kevin to prepare three buffer scenarios with costs, lena to validate regional availability and lead-times, caroline to draft sales tables and negotiation script. I'll assemble proposal and send to DeltaForge by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
